8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":2,"verseId":22,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Motion","totalVerses":25,"verseData":{"id":"v2_22","number":22,"title":"The Mover Cannot Pre-Exist Motion","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"The motion by means of which a mover is manifest Cannot be the motion by means of which he moves. He does not exist before that motion. So what and where is the thing that moves?"},"philosophy":{"insight":"The motion that IDENTIFIES something as a mover cannot be the same motion the mover then PERFORMS. But the mover doesn't exist before being identified. So \"what and where\" is this mover? It's unfindable — neither prior to nor simultaneous with the motion that defines it.","madhyamaka":"Garfield: the verse distinguishes \"identifying motion\" (what makes X a mover) from \"performed motion\" (what X does). These can't be the same motion (that would be the v.9 tautology). But the mover doesn't pre-exist the identifying motion — so it has no prior ground. Kalupahana: \"what and where\" is a powerful rhetorical question revealing the unfindability of an inherently existing mover.","quantum":"Wave Function Collapse / Pre-Measurement Indeterminacy: Before measurement, a particle's properties (position, momentum) are not definite — the particle doesn't \"exist\" in a classical sense at any particular location. The measurement both reveals AND constitutes the state. The particle doesn't pre-exist the measurement that defines it.","bridge":"Both show the \"thing\" doesn't pre-exist the process that defines it. A particle doesn't have a definite position before measurement. A mover doesn't exist before the motion that makes it a mover. In both cases, the entity is constituted by the process, not prior to it.","accessible":"Does a \"winner\" exist before winning? No — you BECOME a winner BY winning. The winning makes you a winner, not the other way around. Similarly, motion makes something a mover — the mover doesn't exist before the motion.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, entities move through space from point A to point B. Ultimately, the mover is not identical to motion, nor different from it — the relation transcends both identity and difference.","commonMisconception":"Not claiming the mover/motion relation is mysteriously unknowable. It's showing that the relation cannot be captured by EITHER identity or difference — both frameworks fail."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Wave Function Collapse / Pre-Measurement Indeterminacy","score":89,"strength":"High","explanation":"Particles don't have definite properties before measurement — the measurement constitutes the state. But if they're different, you need TWO motions (v.5 regress). Either way, inherent motion fails.","realLifeExample":"If \"being a teacher\" IS \"teaching,\" then \"a teacher teaches\" is tautological. But if they're separate, a teacher needs one teaching to be a teacher AND another to actually teach — absurd duplication."},{"q":"Why doesn't the mover exist before motion?","a":"Because \"mover\" is a designation that requires motion. It's a process (circumference) without an inherent origin point."},{"q":"Does this connect to the Buddhist doctrine of dependent origination?","a":"Directly.
